## Introduction

This document demonstrates how to integrate Markdown text directly with dynamic Python code chunks and interactive visualization libraries.

## Interactive Visualization

Below is an interactive scatter plot using **Plotly**. Quarto automatically embeds the interactive JavaScript dependencies into the output HTML without exposing raw code unless toggled.

```{python}
#| label: fig-interactive-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Interactive relationship between dataset variables"
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio

# Required for Plotly to render correctly to HTML from VS Code's notebook engine
pio.renderers.default = "plotly_mimetype+notebook_connected"

# Generate sample dataset
np.random.seed(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'x_metric': np.random.randn(100).cumsum(),
    'y_metric': np.random.randn(100).cumsum(),
    'category': np.random.choice(['Group A', 'Group B', 'Group C'], 100),
    'size': np.random.randint(10, 50, 100)
})

# Build interactive plot
fig = px.scatter(
    df,
    x='x_metric',
    y='y_metric',
    color='category',
    size='size',
    title="Sample Dynamic Trajectory",
    template="plotly_white"
)

fig.show()
```
